questions.q: What real gap does a Unity Catalog volume fill, first flagged in Lesson 8?
options: Volumes replace the need for Delta tables entirely
DBFS root doesn't support reading CSV files
DBFS root has no Unity Catalog governance at all — a volume is governed, addressable file storage that does
DBFS root cannot store any files larger than 1GB
questions.explain: A volume lives inside a schema and is subject to the exact same GRANT/REVOKE mechanism as any table.

questions.q: What is the real path shape for a file stored in a volume?
options: /Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<volume>/<file> — a fourth level under the catalog.schema namespace
dbfs:/FileStore/<file>, exactly like DBFS root
Volumes don't have a defined path shape
/mnt/<volume>/<file>, exactly like a classic mount
questions.explain: This is a genuine fourth level, specifically for files rather than tables, under Lesson 39's namespace.

questions.q: How does the managed/external distinction for volumes compare to Lesson 41's tables?
options: Volumes have no managed/external distinction at all
The distinction only applies to tables, not volumes
It's the exact same idea — a managed volume's location is chosen by Unity Catalog, an external volume points at a location you specify
All volumes are external by default and cannot be managed
questions.explain: External volumes are for files that need to stay reachable outside Databricks too.

questions.q: Does reading a file from a volume require different code than reading from any other path?
options: No — spark.read and dbutils.fs work on a volume path exactly the way they worked on any other path
Volumes cannot be read using PySpark at all
Yes, but only dbutils.fs works, not spark.read
Yes, an entirely new API is required for volume paths
questions.explain: What changes is governance — access is controlled by READ VOLUME/WRITE VOLUME grants, not the reading code itself.

questions.q: Where should Autoloader's incoming CSVs (from Lesson 32) belong now, according to this lesson?
options: They must stay in DBFS root permanently
Volumes cannot be used as an Autoloader source
They should be moved to a Unity Catalog table directly, skipping files entirely
In a volume, instead of DBFS root or an unmanaged mount
questions.explain: This is exactly the real-world replacement path this lesson describes for bronze's incoming files.
